settings.headline: Volunteers on the Hather since 1974
settings.subtitle: Hathermouth River Rescue is a fictional, independent volunteer rescue charity covering twelve miles of the River Hather, from Hather Weir to the Bar where it meets the sea.

settings.headline: How it started
settings.body:
In the winter of 1973 two boys went through the ice on the mill pond. They were pulled out by men from the boatyard with a ladder and a rope. That spring the boatyard, the fire station and the sailing club put up $1,900 for a second-hand inflatable and a shed by the slipway.

Fifty-two years later the charity has two inshore lifeboats, a flood rescue boat, a response vehicle and 63 volunteers. It is still run by the people who launch the boats.
settings.note: Hathermouth River Rescue, the River Hather, the town and everyone named on this site are invented for a Raytha example. Phone numbers use the 555 range.

settings.headline: Trustees
settings.intro: The board meets four times a year. Trustees are unpaid and are elected at the annual general meeting.
settings.foot: Minutes, board papers and the risk register are published to trustees in the trustees' area.
